rule: Resting-HR trend = median of the last 7 days minus median of the baseline window (v1)
summary: Monitoring literature agrees that single-day cardiac readings are too noisy and that multi-day averages (plateau at 3-4 valid days per week) are needed; the 7-day window matches HRV practice. Using a median rather than a mean is a statistical choice (robust to one sick/late night) rather than something tested in athletes, but it only makes the rule harder to trip on one outlier. Overreaching-related RHR shifts are small and can sit inside day-to-day noise, which argues for smoothing, not against it.

sources.note: Ln rMSSD averaged over >=3-4 days per week reached the same signal as 7-day averages; single days were weaker (HRV, applied by analogy to RHR)
Short-term overload raised resting HR only modestly (SMD 0.55); changes may fall within day-to-day variability, so single days mislead
Once-weekly isolated readings missed changes that weekly means detected, due to wide day-to-day variability
